_note: Structural layer first: pledge-works already produces its three registers in every sampled run, so semantic judges are built only where the code checks leave gaps.

structural.bar: opens with a direct answer to the decision or question the user asked, which the rest of the output supports
structural.desc: the output opens with an Answer section

structural.bar: lists the figures and facts about the user's situation it relies on in an Evidence Ledger, typed user-supplied / sourced / assumption / unknown, and invents none
structural.desc: the output has an Evidence Ledger

structural.bar: lists the figures and facts about the user's situation it relies on in an Evidence Ledger, typed user-supplied / sourced / assumption / unknown, and invents none
structural.desc: every Evidence Ledger Type is one of the four allowed words

structural.bar: produces minimum 6 pledges (3 Simple + 2 Responsible Stories + 1 To Whom)
structural.desc: the Pledge Register holds at least 6 pledges

structural.bar: produces minimum 6 pledges (3 Simple + 2 Responsible Stories + 1 To Whom)
every Responsible Story includes a "because" clause naming a value
structural.desc: every Responsible Story has a because-clause

structural.bar: every pledge has all five operationalization fields: quantitative success indicator, quantitative failure signal, named owner
structural.desc: every pledge owner is a named role, not 'the team'

structural.bar: identifies which pledges are default-challenging vs. merely affirming
structural.desc: every pledge is marked default-challenging or affirming

structural.bar: produces a "What We Refuse to Build" red-line register with 3-5 concrete feature-level refusals
produces a "What We Refuse to Build" red-line register with 3-5 concrete feature-level refusals, each with a named owner with veto authority
structural.desc: every red line has a named veto owner

structural.bar: produces a "What We Refuse to Build" red-line register ... and a consequence for breach
structural.desc: every red line states a consequence for breach

structural.bar: produces a Pledge-to-Product traceability table mapping each pledge to a specific product decision
structural.desc: every pledge in the register has a traceability row

structural.bar: a Pledge Register is produced for ongoing maintenance

semantic.bar: every pledge has all five operationalization fields: quantitative success indicator (with number/threshold), quantitative failure signal (with breach threshold)
semantic.instructions: Could someone check `items[{i}]` against real data and say unambiguously whether it was met or breached?

criteria.true: States a measurable threshold -- a number or percentage ('95% of offers', '> 5% in a rolling week'), an absolute ('zero identifiable records leave'), or a specific event whose single occurrence counts ('any feature released without the checklist').
criteria.false: A direction or aspiration with no threshold, such as 'users feel more respected', 'improved accessibility over time', or 'fewer complaints'.
